newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League says Iraq not on meeting agenda.
newsitem.headline: Arab League says Iraq not on meeting agenda.

text.p: The Arab League said on Thursday it would not discuss American threats of another air strike on Iraq during a weekend ministerial meeting in spite of strong regional condemnation of previous U.S. attacks.
"There is nothing about this matter on the agenda, it has not been tabled among the 46 issues that will be discussed," League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel Meguid told reporters.
"It has not been requested by the Iraqi government but if it is raised by the Iraqi delegate, then it is his right," he added after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
But diplomats said the issue was bound to be raised during Saturday's routine six-monthly meeting.

Although Iraq is not invited to an informal foreign ministers' meeting on Friday to follow up resolutions of June's Cairo pan-Arab summit, other states would probably bring it up on the meeting's fringes, they said.

Saturday's routine meeting, which will discuss setting up an Arab court of justice and freeing the Middle East from weapons of mass destruction, will be followed by an emergency meeting aimed at drafting a united stand on recent developments in Arab-Israeli relations.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who along with Egypt called for the meeting, will try to persuade the Arabs to reconsider normalising relations with Israel if it fails to keep its peace pledges which include handing over occupied Arab land in return for peace.

The Palestinians want implementation of the 1993 Oslo agreement on an Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron and other areas of the West Bank, and the opening of a passage for Palestinians to travel between the West Bank and Gaza.
Israel has stressed that self-rule in the Gaza Strip and West Bank cannot go ahead unless its security needs are satisfied.
